hook_text: A drawing nobody can read is a part nobody can make. Three views, in the right places, with the right lines and numbers.
clip_script: First angle orthographic projection, the South African standard. Front view first, the most detailed face. Top view directly below it. View from the right drawn on the left. Line them up with projection lines, pick a scale and write it down. Thick lines for edges you see, dashes for hidden edges, chain lines through hole centres. Dimensions once each, outside the shape, overalls first, then positions from one datum edge, then diameters and radii, all in millimetres. Title block in the corner with name, scale, material and the little cone symbol. For a plastic item add a section cut through the part, hatched, showing the wall thickness and ribs, and show the taper on the sides and the rounded corners. Then check: positions, alignment, lines, dimensions, section, title block. If a friend can describe it without seeing it, it is done.
visual_style: Whiteboard three boxes placed in first angle with projection lines; a line-type key; a dimensioned front view; a hatched section with a thin wall and rib; a title block with the cone symbol.
pacing: Positions, alignment, lines, dimensions, title block, section, check.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the three views of a bottle cap in first angle, with one dimension on each view.
